title: Chhath Puja 2026 Travel Guide: Dates, Places and Plan
summary: A full Chhath Puja 2026 travel guide with the exact dates, the long weekend structure, best ghat cities across Bihar and UP, and a workable plan.
body_markdown:
Chhath is one of the few Indian festivals where the calendar decides everything. The Sandhya Arghya has to happen on the sixth day after Diwali. The vratti has to be at the ghat as the sun sets. Miss the date and there is no second version of it a week later. So the travel around Chhath is not general holiday travel. It is a plan built backwards from two specific moments on two specific days.


## **What This Guide Sets Out to Do**


This article covers the exact Chhath Puja 2026 travel window, the way the long weekend falls this year, the ghat cities worth planning your presence at, and the sequence that keeps the trip aligned with the ritual dates rather than the other way around.


The specific timings and the ghat congestion patterns matter here in a way they do not for other festivals. You can check current bus schedules to the main hubs on the[Varanasi bus booking page](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/varanasi-bus-booking-online) and fix the outbound leg well before the crush.


# **Chhath Puja 2026 Travel: The Full Plan, Day by Day**


Chhath demands more preparation than almost any other Indian festival, and the travel is the part most families spend the least time thinking about. This guide inverts that. It starts with the exact 2026 calendar, layers in the long weekend structure, then moves into the cities and the day by day plan that gets you home in time and back without regret.


## **The Chhath Puja 2026 Calendar**


The festival runs across four days in November 2026. Nahay Khay opens the fast on Friday, November 13. Kharna, when the day long fast breaks with the kheer offering, is Saturday, November 14. The main Sandhya Arghya, the evening offering to the setting sun, is Sunday, November 15. Usha Arghya to the rising sun closes the observance on Monday, November 16.


Two of these dates carry the ritual weight for the vratti: the Sandhya Arghya on Sunday evening and the Usha Arghya on Monday morning. Everything else in the plan, including the travel, is arranged so the observer is at the ghat on time for both.


## **Why the 2026 Long Weekend Actually Helps**


The Chhath Puja 2026 travel window has a specific advantage: the Sandhya Arghya falls on a Sunday and the Usha Arghya on a Monday, which is a public holiday in Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern UP. That combination means most families can travel out on Friday evening or Saturday, arrive in time for Kharna, and return on Tuesday or later without extra leave.


For those working outside the region, one additional leave day on Tuesday November 17 stretches the whole thing into a proper five day break, which is enough to include the extended family, cook the prasad without rushing, and travel back on a quieter weekday. Planning that leave now, in September, is easier than trying to swap dates with a colleague in early November when everyone else has already put their hand up.


## **The Best Cities to Observe Chhath**


The ghat you choose is often the ghat your family has always chosen, and that stays fixed. For anyone with flexibility, or for travellers planning to witness the festival somewhere new, the following cities carry the strongest Chhath character.


### **Patna**


Patna is the definitive Chhath city. The Ganga ghats through the capital, from Gandhi Ghat to Digha and Kollector Ghat, host organised gatherings on a scale that no other city matches. The city administration blocks the surrounding roads on the Arghya evenings, sets up temporary lighting and drinking water stations, and the whole ghat belt turns into one continuous festival ground.


### **Varanasi**


Varanasi’s ghats need no introduction, and they take on a distinct character during Chhath. Assi Ghat and Dashashwamedh Ghat are the busiest, but the smaller ghats through Panchganga and Bhainsasur draw devoted local crowds. The city has published a broader travel context in the[Varanasi seasonal guide](https://www.zingbus.com/blog/best-time-to-visit-varanasi/) , useful if you plan to spend a few extra days in the city.


### **Prayagraj, Ayodhya and Gaya**


Prayagraj brings the Sangam, which turns Chhath into a confluence event with a specific spiritual weight. Ayodhya’s Saryu ghats, freshly redeveloped, have grown into a major Chhath draw in the past two years. Gaya on the Falgu adds a pilgrimage layer, since the river carries its own sanctity beyond the festival itself.


### **Gorakhpur and Lucknow**


Eastern UP has its own Chhath rhythm. Gorakhpur’s Rapti ghats and the Ramgarh Taal draw large gatherings from the surrounding districts, while Lucknow’s Gomti ghats, particularly around Jhulelal Vatika, have become the natural focal points for the Purvanchali community settled in the city.


## **The Travel Plan Backwards from the Ghat**


Because the ritual times fix everything, the sensible way to build a Chhath Puja 2026 travel plan is backwards from the Sandhya Arghya on Sunday evening. The vratti and immediate family need to be at the ghat by mid afternoon on November 15 at the latest, so the arrival at the destination city should ideally be complete by the end of Kharna on Saturday, November 14.


Working back further, that means an overnight bus leaving Delhi on Friday November 13 or the very early hours of Saturday, allowing a Saturday morning arrival, a full day for Kharna preparations and the setting up of the daura basket, then Sunday for the fast and the Arghya. For families not observing the fast but travelling to be present, a Saturday overnight arriving Sunday morning still works, but leaves less breathing room.


## **The Return Journey and Why Not to Rush It**


The Usha Arghya on Monday morning is the emotional close of the festival, and the temptation is to catch a bus back Monday evening. Everyone else has the same thought. Return demand from Bihar and eastern UP peaks between Monday night and Tuesday morning, with fares climbing and seats disappearing early.


If your work allows it, a return on Tuesday night or Wednesday spreads you clear of the return rush, and gives the vratti a day to actually recover from four days of fasting before travelling back. Book the return leg at the same time as the outbound leg, since planning the departure without also planning the way home is what leaves most people stranded on shared cabs at inflated fares.


## **For the Vratti Versus for the Family**


A Chhath Puja 2026 travel plan looks different depending on who in the group is observing the fast. The vratti needs the strictest timing and the least disturbance, so travel comfort matters more than usual: a sleeper berth, a route with a bio washroom on longer legs, and a hub arrival that connects easily to the ghat side of the town.


For accompanying family, the schedule has more flexibility. Some can arrive earlier and help with the ghat prep, others can arrive Saturday and manage food and logistics at the home. Splitting the travel across a couple of departures within the same family is often more practical than trying to move everyone on one bus.


## **Booking Early Is the Whole Trick**


Trains fill months ahead for this window. That is not an exaggeration, and it applies to every route into Bihar and eastern UP. Buses add capacity on the main Delhi corridors, but even those tighten sharply in the two weeks before the festival. The single most useful action, if you are reading this in September or October, is to book the seat now while the choice is still yours.


Fares climb with demand across the two weeks before, so an early booking also protects the budget. If your dates are still uncertain, book a flexible fare on the outbound leg first and confirm the return once your work calendar settles. The point is to lock in the outbound, since that is the leg that decides whether you are at the ghat on Sunday evening at all.


## **Getting There, and Getting the Details Right**


The travel around Chhath is not complicated once you accept that the calendar drives it. The dates are fixed. The vratti has to be at the ghat at specific moments. Everything else, the outbound date, the arrival city, the return, is planned so those moments happen without stress.


Fix the outbound now, plan the return for a quieter day, and let the rest of the week be about the festival itself. Once the seats are booked and the ghat is chosen, the rest of the plan writes itself, and the family can focus on what the four days are actually for.


## **Chhath Puja 2026 Travel Questions**


The questions below cover what travellers ask most often when planning the Chhath week.


### **What are the exact Chhath Puja 2026 dates?**


The exact Chhath Puja 2026 travel dates run November 13 to 16: Nahay Khay on the 13th, Kharna on the 14th, Sandhya Arghya on Sunday the 15th, and Usha Arghya on the 16th.


### **When is the main Chhath Arghya in 2026?**


The main Sandhya Arghya is Sunday, November 15, 2026, when devotees offer prayers to the setting sun, and the Usha Arghya to the rising sun follows on Monday morning.


### **Is Chhath 2026 a long weekend?**


Yes, with Sandhya Arghya on Sunday November 15 and the November 16 holiday, it forms a natural long weekend. One extra leave day on the 17th extends it further.


### **When should I leave for a Chhath Puja 2026 travel plan?**


Aim to reach your ghat city by the end of Kharna on Saturday, November 14. That means an outbound bus on Friday night November 13, arriving Saturday morning at the latest.


### **Which is the best city to observe Chhath?**


Patna’s Ganga ghats host the largest Chhath gatherings in the country, followed by Varanasi, Prayagraj’s Sangam, Ayodhya’s Saryu, Gaya’s Falgu, and the ghats at Gorakhpur and Lucknow.


### **Why is train booking so difficult during Chhath?**


Trains to Bihar and eastern UP fill months in advance for Chhath, with long waitlists. Buses add capacity on the main Delhi corridors and become the realistic road option.


### **How early should I book for Chhath 2026?**


Book as early as September or early October. Seats and fares on every mode tighten sharply in the two weeks before November 13, and last minute bookings are risky.


### **When is the best day to travel back after Chhath?**


Return on Tuesday November 17 or later. Monday night is the peak return rush, and travelling a day later gives the vratti recovery time and usually means better fares.


### **Which Delhi routes carry the heaviest Chhath rush?**


Delhi to Patna, Delhi to Varanasi, Delhi to Gorakhpur and Delhi to Lucknow carry the heaviest Chhath outbound rush, most operating as overnight journeys to save daytime.


### **Should the vratti travel differently from the rest of the family?**


Yes, prioritise comfort for the vratti with a sleeper berth and a smooth arrival. The rest of the family has more flexibility on timing and can arrive across different departures.


### **What should I carry for the Chhath ghat visit?**


Carry a valid government photo ID for travel, the daura basket items or arrange them locally, warm clothing for the pre dawn Usha Arghya, and appropriate footwear for the ghat.


### **Can I plan Chhath 2026 travel with just weekend leave?**


Yes, the Friday November 13 to Monday November 16 window works without extra leave. One additional Tuesday leave gives more breathing room and a smoother return journey.
